_note: French tongue twisters (virelangues) for /virelangues, all traditional folk rhymes passed on orally in France (public domain; no author, no copyright). Each one is first read out (slowly, then at speed), then the learner repeats it and gets points per word, the same scoring as /verification-prononciation. focus: sound ids from src/lib/ausspracheTipps.js. hint: what the twister means, in simple English. Ids are the old slot ids (content-plan §1.3) and no longer describe the twister; this set has 16 (quality over quantity: only twisters known from oral tradition). Question marks stand right behind the last word (the text is scored word by word). `audio` is set to true once public/audio/zungenbrecher/<id>-langsam.mp3 and <id>.mp3 exist; until then the browser voice (fr-FR) reads them. mini (optional): an animal in the twister, so a small Mini-Crew sticker (src/lib/minis.js) sits on the card. mascot (optional): the same with an animal of the crew. dialect (optional): the same twister in a regional accent, voiced as <id>-<slug(dialect.name)>.mp3, only for listening and never scored; none in this set.

sentences.hint: Cooked plums, raw plums. Watch cuits (u) and crus (u): both have the French u.

sentences.text: Le ver vert va vers le verre vert.
sentences.hint: The green worm goes towards the green glass. ver, vert, vers and verre sound the same.

sentences.text: Natacha n'attacha pas son chat Pacha qui s'échappa.
sentences.hint: Natacha didn't tie up her cat Pacha, who ran away.
A saying: fish without a drink is poison. poisson and boisson have ss (s), poison has one s between vowels (z).

sentences.text: Fruits frais, fruits frits, fruits cuits, fruits crus.
sentences.hint: Fresh fruit, fried fruit, cooked fruit, raw fruit. The final s and t are silent.

sentences.text: Si six scies scient six cyprès, six cent six scies scient six cent six cyprès.
sentences.hint: If six saws saw six cypress trees, six hundred and six saws saw six hundred and six cypress trees. On its own, six is said “sis”, but before a consonant the x is silent: six scies is “si si”.

sentences.text: Trois gros rats gris grignotaient trois gros grains d'orge.
sentences.hint: Three big grey rats were nibbling three big grains of barley. No liaison here: trois and gros are always followed by a consonant, so their s is silent.

sentences.text: Didon dîna, dit-on, du dos d'un dodu dindon.
sentences.hint: Dido had dinner, they say, off the back of a plump turkey. Don't say the n of on and don.
Five dogs are chasing six cats. cinq chiens: many people say the q here; six chats: the x is silent before a consonant.

sentences.text: Ton thé t'a-t-il ôté ta toux?
sentences.hint: Has your tea taken your cough away? The -t- in a-t-il is only there to link the vowels.
The convent's hens are sitting on their eggs. couvent is both a noun (convent, said “couvan”) and a verb (they sit on eggs, said “couv”): the -ent of a plural verb is silent.

sentences.text: Gros gras grain d'orge, tout gros gras grain d'orge, tout grand gras grain d'orge.
sentences.hint: Big fat grain of barley, every big fat grain of barley, every tall fat grain of barley.

sentences.text: Un chasseur sachant chasser doit savoir chasser sans son chien.
sentences.hint: A hunter who knows how to hunt must know how to hunt without his dog. Watch the difference between ch (sh) and s.

sentences.text: Je veux et j'exige d'exquises excuses.
sentences.hint: I want and I demand exquisite apologies. exquises and excuses both start with ex- and have an s that is hard to keep sharp.

sentences.text: Trois tortues trottaient sur un trottoir très étroit.
sentences.hint: Three turtles were trotting on a very narrow pavement. Three t's, three r's, and trois trottaient has no liaison: trois tortues, but un trottoir.

sentences.text: Les chaussettes de l'archiduchesse sont-elles sèches, archi-sèches?
sentences.hint: Are the archduchess's socks dry, extra dry? The classic French tongue twister. archi- means extra, very.
